name: Accure laser (1726 nm)

lead: Accure is a clinic laser using a 1726 nm wavelength that targets sebaceous (oil) glands. The payoff people want is less oil production and fewer breakouts in persistent acne, similar to Aviclear.

The wavelength is described as selective for sebaceous glands, aiming at oil production rather than the whole skin surface. Trial registrations show a completed 104-participant device study for acne and a 30-participant laser study, though outcomes are not reported in the registry entries.

paras: It is performed by clinicians in a series of in-office sessions spaced over weeks, usually by people whose acne has persisted despite other approaches. Results are judged over the following months as oil production changes.
Side effects were not reported in the sources reviewed. Cost and availability vary by clinic, and the treatment is only offered in clinical settings.

angle.text: Accure is an in-office 1726 nm laser used to shrink the oil glands behind persistent acne, so there is less sebum and fewer breakouts. Registered trials exist, with outcomes not yet reported in the registry entries.

lead: Accure is a laser procedure that targets sebaceous (oil) glands with a 1726 nm wavelength as a treatment for acne. It belongs to the same class of selective sebaceous-gland lasers as Aviclear [1][2].

Source material for this article is limited to trial registrations. They show a completed 104-participant device study for acne [2] and a 30-participant laser study for acne [1]. Outcomes are not reported in the registry entries.

paras: A registered device study of a laser for acne began in 2020 with 104 participants and is listed as completed [2]. A second laser study for acne vulgaris, started in 2022 with 30 participants, has unknown status [1]. Registered studies of the related Aviclear laser have also been listed for hidradenitis suppurativa (8 participants, completed) [3] and for facial papules in frontal fibrosing alopecia (10 participants, recruiting) [4]. A 10-person study is testing a topical antioxidant with a series of laser procedures to reduce sebum [5]. Registry entries do not report results.
